newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda takes bigger stake in US sales unit.
newsitem.headline: Mazda takes bigger stake in US sales unit.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Friday it raised its stake in Mazda Motor of America Inc (MMA), its import and wholesale unit in the United States, by increasing MMA's capital.

The capital of MMA, located in Irvine, California, was raised to $166 million from $40 million by its allocation of 5.63 million new shares worth $126 million to Mazda. This brought Mazda's ownership to 87.95 percent from 50 percent. Money for the shares came from Mazda's internal funds, a Mazda spokesman said.

MMA was previously owned 50 percent by Mazda, 21 percent by Itochu Corp, 19 percent by Sumitomo Corp and the rest by smaller Japanese investors. Ownership by Itochu now falls to 4.56 percent and that by Sumitomo to 5.08 percent.
Mazda's increase of its stake in MMA is aimed at strengthening MMA's financial structure and providing a base from which to make the business grow.
MMA's sales in calendar 1995 stood at $4.49 billion.
Mazda's car sales in the United States in the January-November period fell 15.9 percent from the same period a year earlier to 223,445 units, the spokesman said.
